messages:
jamie: Heads-up — getting intermittent 5xx from the gpu-allocator headless service in eu-central-1, looks like pods on certain AZ nodes lose connectivity and fall back to public egress (cost spike). Only affects pods scheduled on k8s-eu-gpu-*-spot nodes.

ana: Any infra changes this morning? kube-proxy or controller-manager?

jamie: We pushed a kube-proxy canary (1.27->1.28, ipvs opt-in) around 07:10 and bumped controller-manager affinity to avoid spot contention. Suspect a topology labeling mismatch. Quick repro: inside an affected pod DNS resolves the headless svc to a set of IPs, but connections to some IPs hang.

liam: Can you paste the endpointslice output and kube-proxy log from an affected node? Topology-aware filtering will drop endpoints if labels don't match node zone.

jamie: Sure — pasted snippets below.

jamie: ```shell
$ kubectl get endpointslice -n inference -l kubernetes.io/service-name=gpu-allocator -o wide
NAME                         ADDRESSTYPE   PORTS   AGE   ENDPOINTS   TOPOLOGY
es-abcde12345                IPv4          9000    2h    10          topology.kubernetes.io/zone=eu-central-1b
es-fghij67890                IPv4          9000    2h    4           (missing topology)
```

jamie: kube-proxy log from k8s-eu-gpu-03 (affected):

jamie: ```
I0407 07:45:12.123456 1 proxier.go:123] SyncEndpoints: service gpu-allocator headless -> filtering endpoints by topology for node zone eu-central-1a
I0407 07:45:12.123789 1 proxier.go:456] Filtered endpoints: 4 -> 0 (no matching topology labels)
W0407 07:45:13.000012 1 conntrack.go:89] failed to find healthy backend for 10.2.4.77:9000 -> falling back to external egress
```

ana: That log line nails it — one EndpointSlice is missing topology labels so nodes in eu-central-1a see zero endpoints locally and send traffic out. Likely root cause: endpointSlice controller didn't add topology due to transient leader-election/stall during the controller-manager canary change.

liam: For quick mitigation: 1) add the missing topology label to the EndpointSlice(s) that are missing it, 2) restart kube-proxy on the affected nodes (systemctl restart kube-proxy or drain+uncordon), or 3) roll back the kube-proxy canary. Which do you want to try?

jamie: I patched the EndpointSlice with `kubectl label endpointslice es-fghij67890 topology.kubernetes.io/zone=eu-central-1a -n inference` and restarted kube-proxy on the 3 affected nodes. Traffic recovered and 5xx count dropped to baseline. Cost spike reversed.

infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-042 (gpu-allocator endpointslice topology mismatch) — Pager duty notified.

ana: Postmortem action items:
- Open issue to add an e2e that exercises EndpointSlice topology propagation during controller-manager leader changes.
- Add a check in our rollout playbook to verify EndpointSlice topology labels after controller-manager or kube-proxy upgrades.
- Roll back kube-proxy canary until we have a verified plan for ipvs + topology testing.

liam: Also propose an alert: EndpointSlice topology imbalance for headless services (threshold: >50% of nodes in an AZ observing zero local endpoints for a ready service) — will draft.

jamie: Thanks — noted. I've assigned follow-ups in the incident ticket and pinned the quick patch commands to the incident thread. We'll coordinate a controlled kube-proxy re-roll after validation in staging. :thumbsup:

ana: Good recovery. Leaving the ticket open for the postmortem and the rollout gating change.
